html:
Emperor of the eastern Roman empire from 408 to 450, one of the longest reigns in Roman history. He was crowned as a baby in 402 by his father Arcadius and became sole emperor at seven. His sister Pulcheria, his ministers and later his wife Eudocia did much of the ruling.

His reign left lasting works:

  • The Theodosian Walls, built in his youth, which guarded Constantinople for a thousand years.
  • A state school in the capital, the University of Constantinople, in 425.
  • The Theodosian Code of 438, the first official collection of imperial laws.

He was pious and known for his fine handwriting, hence his nickname. Church quarrels over the nature of Christ marked his rule: the Council of Ephesus in 431 condemned Nestorius. He paid Attila large sums in gold to keep the Huns away. He died in 450 after falling from his horse.
